sense.text:
“Thou shalt have no other gods before me.” That is the first commandment, and the Catholic Church keeps it first.

But their own indoctrination manual, the Convert’s Catechism of Catholic Doctrine, and the Catholic list of the ten commandments online, number them differently from God’s book. Laid side by side with Exodus 20, you can see exactly what Esau and his Catholic Church did to God’s holy commandments.

“Thou shalt not make unto thee any graven image.” That is the second commandment, and it is the one the Catholic Church crossed out of its list.

They removed God’s second commandment so they could fill their churches with idols and worship them without a conscience. The Catholic Church is the mother of all the Christian churches and denominations, and that is the idolatry all of them came out of.

“Thou shalt not take the name of the Lord thy God in vain” is the third commandment. With the second one gone, the Catholic list moves this one up to second, and everything after it slides up one place.

“Remember the sabbath day, to keep it holy.” In God’s book the Sabbath is the fourth commandment. In the Catholic catechism it is called the third, and the online Catholic list has changed it to keeping holy the Lord’s day.

Their own catechism says plainly that they observe Sunday instead of Saturday because the Catholic Church, at the council of Laodicea, transferred the solemnity from Saturday to Sunday. It says they made the change because Christ rose on a Sunday and the Holy Ghost came down on the apostles on a Sunday, at Pentecost. Their own Cardinal Gibbons wrote that you can read the Bible from Genesis to Revelation and not find a single line authorizing the sanctification of Sunday, and that the scriptures enforce the observance of Saturday, a day they never sanctify.

So there is no commandment for a Sunday Sabbath. In the Christian church the authority is not the Bible, it is the pope and your pastor, and that is why the world worships on Sunday.

The council of Laodicea, held in Phrygia, ruled in canon 29 that Christians must not Judaize by resting on the Saturday Sabbath. They told believers to do their regular work on the seventh day, to honor Sunday as the Lord’s day instead, and they declared anyone caught keeping the Saturday Sabbath anathema: cut off, excommunicated from Christ. Judaizing just means obeying the commandments of God and following the Bible. That is why the sales, the cookouts and the events all land on Saturday. It comes from the Catholic Church, and all the world follows it, straight defiling God’s Sabbath day.

That is how the Catholic Church gets down to this day. In India, where it has a stronghold on our people in the remote villages, the one thing the people spoke of was the fear of the Catholic Church cutting them off from their resources.

“Thou shalt not covet thy neighbour’s house, thou shalt not covet thy neighbour’s wife, nor his manservant, nor his maidservant, nor his ox, nor his ass, nor any thing that is thy neighbour’s.” The house and the wife are both in the one tenth commandment.

The Catholic Church split this one commandment in two, coveting the neighbour’s wife as a ninth and his goods as a tenth, to keep the count at ten after they had removed the commandment against graven images.

precepts.why:
“Forasmuch as this people draw near me with their mouth, and with their lips do honour me.” Our people have a zeal for God. “But have removed their heart far from me”: our mind is removed from the laws of God, the same way the Catholic Church removed the whole second commandment and made up its own Catholic commandments.

“And their fear toward me is taught by the precept of men.” Our fear toward God is taught by the Catholic Church, by the precept of our oppressor, the white man. That is what was seen in India: people who agreed it was an idol and did not believe in it, but would not get rid of it out of fear of the Catholic Church and of this white man.

That is the history: if you kept the laws of God, they would cut you off, because they had a stronghold on the place.

sense.text:
The Sabbath day was changed because the Catholic Church did it at the council of Laodicea, and all the Christian world follows after it. Daniel saw it coming.

“And he shall speak great words against the most High.” We know who the he is: it is the white man. And now we know exactly when he did it, when he decided to speak great words against the Most High concerning his Sabbath day. “And shall wear out the saints of the most High.”

“And think to change times and laws.” It says think, because he did not know that God was going to wake us up in these last days. God would pour out his spirit on his people in the last days, and we would find out that he is a liar from the beginning, like his father the devil. He changed times and laws, particularly the Sabbath day.

“And they shall be given into his hand until a time and times and the dividing of time.”

precepts.why:
“Let no man deceive you by any means: for that day shall not come, except there come a falling away first.” The falling away is us going into slavery. “And that man of sin be revealed, the son of perdition”: Esau is that man of sin, the son of perdition, of destruction.

“Who opposeth and exalteth himself above all that is called God.” We just read it out of their own books: they exalt themselves above God, they changed the Sabbath day, they say what they say is more important than the word of God, and they remixed the ten commandments and handed them to the people. The Catholic Church got a foothold all through Africa, and our people there follow after it, believing these things and worshipping idols just like their oppressor.

“So that he as God sitteth in the temple of God, shewing himself that he is God.” That is what he does: he changes the Sabbath day and then puts up idols to show himself that he is God. He will only be revealed by us revealing him in the last days and opening our people’s eyes. We are the only people that can do it.

“For the mystery of iniquity doth already work: only he who now letteth will let, until he be taken out of the way.” It was already at work in Rome in Paul’s time, before Laodicea ever met: the idolatry, the worshipping of other gods and the subjugating of people, and it was only going to get worse. Paul was warning us in his letters about the time this man would come and show himself that he is God. Once the Lord took us out of hard bondage and we were able to search out the truth, we would find out that this is the man of sin that opposes God: the white man.

A lot of our people are in darkness on this. They refuse to believe that Esau is still on the earth, as if God has future judgments for him but made him extinct in ancient times. It makes no sense; they are blinded by church.

“And he opened his mouth in blasphemy against God, to blaspheme his name.” His name is the word, and changing the Sabbath is blaspheming it. “And his tabernacle, and them that dwell in heaven.” That is why everything in heaven looks like him: the angels, God, Christ, the disciples, the prophets. He shows himself that he is God.

“And it was given unto him to make war with the saints, and to overcome them: and power was given him over all kindreds, and tongues, and nations.” That war was physical and spiritual. He went throughout the world and enslaved and colonized the Israelites, from the western hemisphere where we are now to the eastern hemisphere, all throughout Africa, even the remote islands. The spiritual war is still going on today, but our people are asleep and comfortable in it and do not even know they are at war.

sense.text:
“Even him, whose coming is after the working of Satan with all power and signs and lying wonders.” He got that power from Satan.

People always wonder how a caveman, because that is what Esau is, a hairy beast of a man that came out of the caves, conquered the whole entire world in 250 years. His power came from Satan.

precepts.why:
“Again, the devil taketh him up into an exceeding high mountain, and sheweth him all the kingdoms of the world, and the glory of them; And saith unto him, All these things will I give thee, if thou wilt fall down and worship me.”

The kingdoms of the world and their glory belong to Satan to give. So where did the power come from that this white man has had for the last 250 years in America alone, not counting Rome’s dynasty, the Greeks when they ruled, the Spaniards or Britain? All that power to rule the kingdoms of the world and have the glory of them came from Satan.

The agreement Esau made with Satan to rule over the world is nothing new. It did not start when they got on the Nina, the Pinta and the Santa Maria.

“Hast thou but one blessing, my father? bless me, even me also, O my father. And Esau lifted up his voice, and wept.” Esau is the so-called white man of today; that is his biblical name. He wept and cried for a blessing.

“Behold, thy dwelling shall be the fatness of the earth, and of the dew of heaven from above.” He would live everywhere on the earth, and in the best places. But by what means, a caveman living in the best places all over the world? “And by thy sword shalt thou live.” By the sword.

And who was right there waiting to give him the power to use that sword? Satan himself, ready to bless him with the art of war, to kill, to steal and to destroy. That is what his ancestors did from Greece to Rome, from Spain to Great Britain, all the way up to America today, killing and stealing with the power of Satan behind them and the weapons to rule the entire world. He obtained that blessing by worshipping Satan.

“And no marvel; for Satan himself is transformed into an angel of light.” That is the Catholic Church.

Satan is all throughout the Christian church presenting himself as an angel of light, as if he were God himself and has done the world nothing but good, while he has been all over the world with the sword raping, robbing and killing and taking the best places for himself. No matter where he is, he is in the best places. Go out of the country to black or Latino countries and you will notice Esau never lives with the common, native people. He sits up high on the hills and looks down on the servants.

“And all that dwell upon the earth shall worship him.” Worship who? Esau. They have been indoctrinated and enslaved with his image, and also by war. So they worship Esau, and in turn they are actually worshipping Satan, because he looks like an angel of light to them. They do not know the difference. They do not know that Satan is the one giving this white man power; they think God is behind the things he does.

“Whose names are not written in the book of life of the Lamb slain from the foundation of the world.” But the elect, the chosen of God, are not going to be food. We are going to wake up in these last days with the history and the scriptures, with the prophets going throughout the four corners of the earth, to London, to the Solomon Islands, throughout Africa, wherever we can get to, and wake up the elect whose names are written in the Lamb’s book of life, and they are going to come up out of it.

sense.text: “Now the Spirit speaketh expressly”: that is Christ talking to Paul. “That in the latter times some shall depart from the faith.” The faith is Christ; the faith is this Bible, and some are going to depart from it. “Giving heed to seducing spirits, and doctrines of devils.” Then he explains what the doctrine of a devil is.

“Speaking lies in hypocrisy.” Look up the definition of hypocrisy and watch how it matches Esau, your friendly neighborhood white man: the act of pretending to have moral beliefs, virtues or feelings that you do not actually possess, or telling other people to behave a certain way while doing the exact opposite.

Pretending to have moral beliefs: look up which religion has the most abortions and it is the Christians, and among the Christians, the Catholics are at the top. They have unearthed babies’ bones under where the nuns live, and nuns are not supposed to have no sex. They are hypocrites.

Virtues and feelings they do not possess: they do not love their neighbor as they love themselves, and black and Latino people know it. This white man is all over the world bombing people, but gets mad at Pooky and Ray Ray for black on black crime. That is Christianity, the Catholic Church 101: speaking lies in hypocrisy.

Saying versus doing: they have called black people lazy ever since we left the plantation, when the white man was the lazy one; he was not out in the field with us, and we are the ones that keep America going. False virtue: putting on a show of being good or religious for praise, which is why they put In God We Trust on their money while being the devil the Bible speaks of. The double standard: the white man is the biggest drug dealer on the face of the earth. No negro has a boat to bring in all the dope in America. There are no gun stores in Chicago and no gun makers in Africa, yet guns run all through Chicago, Africa and Haiti. The white man is a liar and a hypocrite.

“Having their conscience seared with a hot iron.”

“Forbidding to marry”: that is Catholic Christianity hands down. “And commanding to abstain from meats, which God hath created to be received with thanksgiving of them which believe and know the truth.” They have something made up called Lent; God never said anything like that. This is speaking of clean foods, and the only time you abstain from clean food is on the day of atonement. That is it.

precepts.why:
“And the Lord shall scatter thee among all people, from the one end of the earth even unto the other.” For the negroes who now say we never were where the slave ships were: stop it. You learned this in school. Now you have Instagram and TikTok accounts and suddenly it is not true anymore. Your ancestors are ashamed of you.

“And there thou shalt serve other gods, which neither thou nor thy fathers have known, even wood and stone.” Those are man-made religions, particularly Christianity and Islam. We have been destroyed through these religions in slavery, to where we now follow after the same hypocrisy, the lies and the loss of virtue this white man has, presenting ourselves as something good while we are full of dead men’s bones inside these religions. It has destroyed us as a people: we departed from the faith into the doctrines of devils.

sense.text:
“My people hath been lost sheep”: we are lost sheep. “Their shepherds have caused them to go astray,” because they teach us the same thing the white man taught his own people, the lies and the hypocrisy. We have taken on those attributes: worshipping idols, making up God as we go, remixing God’s commandments and saying they do not mean what they say but what we can comprehend.

“They have turned them away on the mountains: they have gone from mountain to hill.” We went from being on high to being on the bottom.

“They have forgotten their restingplace.” We forgot our homeland. On social media now, black people in America are saying, I ain’t African, I never been to Africa, as if not going to a place changes your nationality. You can never change what nation of people you belong to. We are not African in the sense of Nilotes or Hamites, but Israel is in northeast Africa, and we want nothing to do with the eastern hemisphere, as if we never came from that side of the earth.

Our current place of captivity, where we have taken our rest, is destroying us. When you read the Bible you are supposed to have a revolutionary spirit to change things when your people are oppressed. What quells that fighting spirit, the lion of Judah in us, is Christianity. It suppresses it until you do not want to fight anymore, because what is better than here?

“All that found them have devoured them.” We have been devoured in politics, in religion, in the justice system, in the school system. Everything in this society takes advantage of us.

“And their adversaries said, We offend not, because they have sinned against the Lord.” They say they did nothing wrong; it is our own fault we grow up like this. Stop using white man talking points to come against your own people. This white man is the devil.

precepts.why:
What happens when you forget your homeland, your resting place? “Arise ye, and depart; for this is not your rest.” America, Babylon the great, all the lands we have been enslaved and colonized in, are not our rest. We should never be comfortable there, because in every one of those places oppression, death and destruction follow behind us. That is why we find no peace and no rest there.

“Because it is polluted, it shall destroy you.” When you get comfortable in the land of your captivity it pollutes you and destroys you, because you begin to take on the attributes of your oppressor. That is not for us. We are God’s children; we cannot take on his ways and make them work for us, it always backfires. The white man has the sword and the power to rule and subjugate the world, but God will not let his children follow after him like the rest of the world and prosper.

“Even with a sore destruction.” That is where we are as a nation of people: in a sore destruction of the mind, from the grown man and grown woman down to the children, because we have gotten comfortable in our captivity and forgotten our homeland. You can hear it in all the opinionated podcasts made with a $30 Amazon kit.

Here is the proof this is not our rest. Nolan Wales’ mother and father will never have rest again; their son is gone, and that case will likely never be solved. Kendrick Johnson’s family has tried for years to get justice. A 29-year-old black woman was found hanging from a tree in Mississippi so high that it would have taken a ladder to get her there, with no ladder at the scene. Rasheem Carter’s mother had to stand and look at his bones. Emmett Till’s accuser only admitted she lied on her deathbed. When you forget your resting place and have no desire to go back to it, the place you are in will destroy you with a sore destruction.

This is for our brothers and sisters that love this society and love this world; it is our downfall as a people.

“Wherefore thus saith the Holy One of Israel, Because ye despise this word, and trust in oppression and perverseness, and stay thereon.” We despise God’s word, we trust in our oppression and stay on it. It is sin for us to trust in this oppression and believe in it.

“Therefore this iniquity shall be to you as a breach ready to fall, swelling out in a high wall, whose breaking cometh suddenly at an instant.” There is no comfort, no protection, no covering for us in assimilating into America, Babylon the great.

“And I am very sore displeased with the heathen that are at ease: for I was but a little displeased.” We did sin, and we deserved to go into captivity. Read Daniel 9 if you disagree: God called out to us by the prophets for thousands of years, and he is righteous in all his judgments.

“And they helped forward the affliction.” But the heathen did too much. He went beyond what was intended for us in slavery; he did more to us than he was supposed to do. That is why the adversaries saying they offend not is a lie.

Why did they go beyond what God intended? “Because thou hast had a perpetual hatred.” It is a perpetual hatred they have for us, going all the way back to Cain and Abel, Jacob and Esau, and today it plays out again as blacks and whites. It has never gone anywhere.

“And hast shed the blood of the children of Israel by the force of the sword in the time of their calamity, in the time that their iniquity had an end.” In every captivity God said, it is time for my people to come home. In Babylon, the Persians had Cyrus let us go back. Under the Greeks, the Maccabees ran them out of the land and we inhabited it again. When Christ walked the earth under Rome, Israelites were back in the land of Judea, not all twelve tribes, but back in our land. But Esau, when our iniquity had an end, refused to let us go and kept shedding our blood. He went beyond what God wanted for us.

Why did he keep shedding our blood when our iniquity had an end? This is for everyone who thinks that smiling white man in your face means to do you good.

“But executing thy judgments upon them by little and little, thou gavest them place of repentance, not being ignorant that they were a naughty generation.” Solomon is speaking of the ancient Egyptians, and this is modern Egypt today. They are a naughty people. “And that their malice was bred in them”: God made them that way; he put that in them. “And that their cogitation would never be changed.” They will never change as a race of people.

That is why the perpetual hatred keeps playing itself out from Cain and Abel to Jacob and Esau to blacks and whites, and Christianity blinds us from accepting what God is telling us. Name a century that black and Latino people have had pure peace around this white man. Pure peace is not getting the vote; it is not having to look over your shoulder when the police get behind you. There is not one. Their own record of atrocities against black Americans runs from the slave trade of 1619 to 1865, to the racial terror after emancipation, to the massacres at Memphis, Colfax in Louisiana, Wilmington, Atlanta, East St. Louis, the Red Summer, Arkansas, Tulsa and Rosewood, through the 1600s, 1700s, 1800s and 1900s. And that is only what was reported; imagine what was not documented.

As a result of all the enslavement and the massacres, Esau thinks he is getting away with it. “These things hast thou done, and I kept silence.” They think, we enslaved the Lord’s people and he did nothing.

“Thou thoughtest that I was altogether such an one as thyself.” That is what Esau thinks to this day. That is why they hold themselves not guilty when they slay us, when they put us into slavery, when they give no reparations. Esau thinks he is God.

“But I will reprove thee, and set them in order before thine eyes.” There will be a judgment for these things, and what is listed is not even all of it.

With all those things listed, the Lord had to get involved for this man not to wipe us off the face of the earth.

“If it had not been the Lord who was on our side, now may Israel say; If it had not been the Lord who was on our side, when men rose up against us”: when Edom rose up against us with his perpetual hatred. “Then they had swallowed us up quick, when their wrath was kindled against us.” He would have destroyed us off the face of the earth quickly.

That is why we have to come back to the commandments of God and learn who we are.

Lamentations 3:22 and Psalms 124 go hand in hand. “It is of the Lord’s mercies that we are not consumed, because his compassions fail not.”

Without him we would have been destroyed by this white man and gone off the face of the earth, because that is his goal and his aim, his perpetual hatred. Go back to Genesis 27: Esau was angry and said in himself that when his father died he would kill his brother, and he has been trying to get that revenge ever since. With all the power on his side from Satan, with all his weapons, ruling the world, while black and Latino people have nothing to protect ourselves behind enemy lines, how do you think we survived to this day? It is the Lord on our side.

So don’t ever think that white man smiling in your face loves you, black woman. And still no peace in any century: the Tuskegee syphilis study from 1932 to 1972, forty years of lying to black men and killing them; the 16th Street Baptist Church bombing in Birmingham in 1963; the murders of our leaders and heroes, Andrew Goodman, James Chaney, Medgar Evers, Dr. Martin Luther King, Malcolm X; and police violence and unequal punishment right on into the 2000s, where a black first-time offender gets 35 years and a white woman who stabbed her black boyfriend to death sits smiling in the courtroom and gets six. But God is merciful; his compassions fail not.

sense.text:
Look at the mercies God gave us in these times. “Therefore thou deliveredst them into the hand of their enemies, who vexed them.” Because of our sins he is justified in doing that.

“And in the time of their trouble, when they cried unto thee, thou heardest them from heaven; and according to thy manifold mercies”, like Lamentations and the Psalms spoke of, “thou gavest them saviours, who saved them out of the hand of their enemies.”

That is the manifold mercy we have today: God sent us saviors to save us out of the hand of our enemies and show us the way we must walk. As the Bishop has said, in every captivity the Lord sent saviors, because he is merciful.

precepts.why:
“And he brought out of him a merciful man, which found favour in the sight of all flesh, even Moses, beloved of God and men, whose memorial is blessed.” A merciful man sent to a people that needed mercy. When we were in Egypt, God sent a savior: Moses.

“He made him like to the glorious saints, and magnified him, so that his enemies stood in fear of him. By his words he caused the wonders to cease, and he made him glorious in the sight of kings, and gave him a commandment for his people, and shewed him part of his glory.”

“Jesus the son of Nave”, which is Joshua, “was valiant in the wars, and was the successor of Moses in prophecies, who according to his name was made great for the saving of the elect of God.” For the saving of the elect, God sent Joshua.

“And taking vengeance of the enemies that rose up against them, that he might set Israel in their inheritance. How great glory gat he, when he did lift up his hands, and stretched out his sword against the cities!”

“Samuel, the prophet of the Lord, beloved of his Lord, established a kingdom, and anointed princes over his people. By the law of the Lord he judged the congregation, and the Lord had respect unto Jacob.” God had respect unto Jacob.

“By his faithfulness he was found a true prophet, and by his word he was known to be faithful in vision.” God sent Samuel.

“And after him rose up Nathan to prophesy in the time of David. As is the fat taken away from the peace offering, so was David chosen out of the children of Israel.”

After Saul failed to do what God commanded, God sent David to lead the children of Israel the right way.

“Then stood up Elias the prophet as fire, and his word burned like a lamp.” Elias is Elijah the prophet, and his word burned literally and spiritually.

“He brought a sore famine upon them, and by his zeal he diminished their number. By the word of the Lord he shut up the heaven, and also three times brought down fire.” That is the literal fire that came down from heaven.

“O Elias, how wast thou honoured in thy wondrous deeds! and who may glory like unto thee!” Elijah was a bad man.

“And of the twelve prophets let the memorial be blessed, and let their bones flourish again out of their place”: let them come back again.

“For they comforted Jacob, and delivered them by assured hope.” The prophets were always sent to deliver the people, because they were created to be saviors.

They were created to be saviors, and they were always “Leaders of the people by their counsels, and by their knowledge of learning meet for the people, wise and eloquent are their instructions.”

They were leaders and saviors because it was in their soul to be. They were ordained to be saviors when our people were in captivity, and God always sent them back when we were in captivity.

That is heavy history, and you may think it is not going to happen today. God always sent saviors to save the people in their captivity.

“For the day of the Lord is near upon all the heathen”: this is talking about now. “As thou hast done, it shall be done unto thee: thy reward shall return upon thine own head.” We have seen all that Esau has done to our people: changing the laws of God, constantly oppressing us, murdering us with no justice and no rest in this captivity. All of it is going to be done to him.

“For as ye have drunk upon my holy mountain.” God’s holy mountain is Jerusalem, and right now the heathen are sitting on it in Israel today. “So shall all the heathen drink continually, yea, they shall drink, and they shall swallow down, and they shall be as though they had not been.” They are going to drink that judgment.

“But upon mount Zion shall be deliverance.” Upon the children of Israel, the blacks, Hispanics, Native Americans and those scattered throughout the diaspora, shall be deliverance.

How is God going to deliver us? “And saviours shall come up on mount Zion to judge the mount of Esau.”

The same thing seen in the time of Moses, of Joshua, of David, is going to happen now. God sent his son Jesus the Christ and the 144,000 to deliver his people from captivity. Even in this captivity, the Lord sent saviors.

sense.text:
The prophets were always leaders of the people, sent as saviors. Meditating on the scriptures through the night, this came: a prophet’s purpose is always greater than his rank. None of them were ever concerned with numbers, only the purpose.

“Also I heard the voice of the Lord, saying, Whom shall I send, and who will go for us? Then said I, Here am I; send me.” Isaiah asked to be sent, to carry out the purpose of God. Read down and he was sent to prophesy destruction to come, and still Isaiah in the spirit said, Send me.

That is the same thing that happens with all the prophets of God sent back as saviors: they all made an agreement with God and said, Send me. Go precept upon precept and you can see how it plays out in the spiritual world and is seen in the physical world.

precepts.why:
“Before I formed thee in the belly I knew thee.” Why did he know him? Because they had a conversation about the mission in heaven before he came upon the earth: who shall I send during this captivity? And Jeremiah said, Send me. I will go down during that time.

“And before thou camest forth out of the womb I sanctified thee, and I ordained thee a prophet unto the nations.” Go down in the time of Babylon and save thy people.

Jeremiah’s orders go on: “See, I have this day set thee over the nations and over the kingdoms, to root out, and to pull down, and to destroy, and to throw down, to build, and to plant.” Tear it down and build it back up. Our people were in the midst of idolatry in the time of Babylon, worshipping trees through Nimrod the same way we do today, and Jeremiah in the heavens told God, Send me, I will be that savior in that time.

“Son of man, I have made thee a watchman unto the house of Israel.” Where was this discussed? In the heavens, before he was formed in the belly. “Therefore hear the word at my mouth, and give them warning from me”: give them warning and save them from the destruction to come.

“When I say unto the wicked, Thou shalt surely die; and thou givest him not warning, nor speakest to warn the wicked from his wicked way, to save his life.” To save his life, because you are going down there to be a savior; you have a purpose upon this earth. “The same wicked man shall die in his iniquity; but his blood will I require at thine hand.”

That is why a prophet’s purpose is greater than his rank: your purpose is to save the lives of the house of Israel. Everywhere we have gone we have been devoured, and it is on you in this captivity to save your people. When you will not fulfil the mission you agreed to in the heavens when you said Send me, God says he will require their blood at your hand.

“Yet if thou warn the wicked, and he turn not from his wickedness, nor from his wicked way, he shall die in his iniquity; but thou hast delivered thy soul.” Why is our soul on the line for the people, when the scripture says every man shall die for his own sin? Because when you understand the word you are a watchman of Israel, and your job is to save the people in this captivity. Their sin becomes yours if you do not speak the word to warn them from their wicked ways. God holds you accountable because you said Send me; you took on that responsibility in the heavens.

This is how it plays out in the earth. “But when it pleased God”: at the appointed time, in whatever captivity it was. “Who separated me from my mother’s womb”: he brought you into the earth. “And called me by his grace, To reveal his Son in me, that I might preach him among the heathen”: that is our people that are scattered. “Immediately I conferred not with flesh and blood.”

At an appointed time upon the earth we begin our mission to be saviors to our people, to be watchmen, to warn them from their wicked ways and tell them to repent and turn back to God that they may save their lives. It happens to all of us who understand that we are Israelites according to the Bible and understand the word of God to the point where we can teach it. God calls us at a specific time in every captivity to be a savior to the people, and that is why their blood is on our hands if we do not warn them of the danger to come and the danger they are living in.

“And now, saith the Lord that formed me from the womb to be his servant.” Again and again a prophet is formed in the womb, because we are in the spirit realm first and come into the earth formed by God Almighty. To be his servant: we agreed to that. “To bring Jacob again to him”: to be saviors.

“Though Israel be not gathered, yet shall I be glorious in the eyes of the Lord, and my God shall be my strength.” The prophets of God are glorious in his eyes. There is no higher calling than being a prophet of the Most High when he has revealed his Son in you at the appointed time. Some of us used to be antios, but once Christ was awakened in us we left all that; we do not glory in it anymore. It does not compare to being watchmen of Israel in these last days. This is the true glory: glorious not to man but to God.

“It is a light thing that thou shouldest be my servant to raise up the tribes of Jacob, and to restore the preserved of Israel.” That is our job. “I will also give thee for a light to the Gentiles”: that is the scattered Israelites. “That thou mayest be my salvation unto the end of the earth”: that you may be a savior.

Many times we as the prophets do not understand the magnitude of our calling. The Lord said he would send us as saviors, and the people’s salvation will come no other way but by the saviors God sent and through his word. By us going forth and teaching God’s word, salvation comes here on earth.

“How then shall they call on him in whom they have not believed? and how shall they believe in him of whom they have not heard? and how shall they hear without a preacher? And how shall they preach, except they be sent?” There is no way for the people to be saved unless the saviors are sent. That is the importance of the prophets.

“As it is written, How beautiful are the feet of them that preach the gospel of peace.”

We have been sent throughout the four corners of the earth; we have been sent from the beginning to be saviors.

“For after that in the wisdom of God the world by wisdom knew not God, it pleased God by the foolishness of preaching to save them that believe.” Our people may see what we do as foolishness, but it pleased God by the foolishness of preaching. That is our purpose: to be sent to preach God’s word to save the believers, to save the elect. That is our mission, and you have to take pride in it.

Look what Paul said through the spirit of Christ: “Wherefore, brethren, covet to prophesy.” We should always covet to teach the people God’s word, because it is glorious in his eyes.

He loves it when we stand on the corner and make fools of ourselves preaching his word, because his word does not go out void. There may not be many people stopping in front of you, but God takes that word, puts it in video form on YouTube, where Esau uses much evil to deceive our people, and it reaches the person it was meant to reach. Crops take time to grow; that is what we are, husbandmen. Ask who came in by a YouTube video, and how long they had been watching: two, three years. The word you taught did not go out void; it bore fruit in its time.

sense.text: Always covet to prophesy. “Thou therefore endure hardness, as a good soldier of Jesus Christ.” Read it in the King James. We are soldiers in the war against evil.

“No man that warreth entangleth himself with the affairs of this life; that he may please him who hath chosen him to be a soldier.” We were chosen by Christ himself to be soldiers in his army against this great evil here in Babylon. The odds may seem stacked against us, but we are tearing down this kingdom one soul at a time; every time we prophesy and someone repents, we get closer to the kingdom. We cannot abandon our post because we do not have the numbers that make us feel good, because a prophet’s purpose is always greater than his rank.

This is the spiritual lesson of a soldier forgetting his mission. A soldier who forgets his mission loses his direction. A soldier is not supposed to live merely for himself, and that is what Paul is reminding Timothy of: you are not here for yourself in this war. Wherever we are in Israel United in Christ, it is not merely for yourself.

He has been given an assignment and is expected to remain focused on it. Nobody in Israel United in Christ gave you that assignment; Christ Almighty, King of Kings, gave it to you, and he expects you to stay focused on it. The danger is becoming so occupied with everyday things that we forget why we were called, getting caught up in numbers.

First, forgetting the mission can cause disobedience: you hear what God instructed you to do and fail to act on it because you are in your emotions. The problem is not forgetting information; it is failing to act on what you were given.

Second, a distracted soldier becomes vulnerable to Satan. When you lose sight of your assignment, distractions take priority over prayer, obedience, righteousness, service, faith and your relationship with God, and you become easy pickings.

Third, forgetting the mission affects other people. A soldier’s assignment is not only about himself; his actions affect the whole unit. God gives different gifts and assignments, the talents and administrations in the body of Christ, but when you become sensual it is all about you. When someone goes down in the body of Christ, others are working double time because they are down a brother or a sister.

Fourth, you can still wear the uniform and forget the mission: standing among the other soldiers with the equipment, but a shell, faking it till you make it, forgetting the goal because you do not have the numbers, and not really among us.

The summation: a soldier must remember his commander, Jesus the Christ, his orders and his mission. A servant of God must remember who called him: God. Who am I serving? God. What are my orders? Teach his word, prophesy. Who am I supposed to serve? Others. And if I forget, I become distracted, disobedient, ineffective, and lose sight of my purpose. The lesson is simple: don’t just remember that you are a soldier; remember what you were sent to do. Not to attain numbers. We were sent down here with a purpose.

precepts.why:
A distracted soldier becomes vulnerable, and Satan is waiting on you to forget the mission at hand.

“Be sober, be vigilant; because your adversary the devil, as a roaring lion, walketh about, seeking whom he may devour.” When you take your eyes off the mission you become weak, and Satan is waiting on that crack in your armor to destroy you and bring you down.

Satan is not going to stand by and let you wake up God’s people. You are out here teaching and prophesying, and he is not going to sit there and allow it. That is why the Lord tells us this.

“My son, if thou come to serve the Lord, prepare thy soul for temptation.” Things are going to happen to hinder you in this truth, and you have to prepare your soul.

“Set thy heart aright”: in this wicked mind comes all manner of wickedness, and we have to set our hearts right to the commandments of God. “And constantly endure”: endure in this truth, which comes with studying, praying and applying, as leadership tells us all the time. “And make not haste in time of trouble”: when those temptations come, do not make haste. We have to endure.

Remember what you were sent to do; you can see it play out in the scriptures.

“Simon, son of Jonas, lovest thou me more than these? He saith unto him, Yea, Lord; thou knowest that I love thee. He saith unto him, Feed my lambs.” If you love me, feed my lambs. The second time: “Feed my sheep.” The third time, “Peter was grieved because he said unto him the third time, Lovest thou me?” “Jesus saith unto him, Feed my sheep.”

Don’t forget: you were chosen to feed my sheep. You made this agreement, this covenant, with him in the heavens before you came to the earth. His commander gave him his orders and repeated them three times to make sure he did not forget them before he left him.

What did Peter do in turn in his letters to the men he was set over? “Feed the flock of God which is among you.” He learned it from his commander and did not forget, and he passed it on, reminding the men under him: feed the flock of God with knowledge and understanding.

“Taking the oversight thereof, not by constraint, but willingly; not for filthy lucre, but of a ready mind.” Have a ready mind to teach and feed our people so they are not deceived by the idiots out here.

One of them says Israelites teach that we are saved by race, not by grace. Nobody teaches that. However jacked up some may be, Israelites teach you have to keep the commandments. He says he could care less about your bloodline, but man might not care and God does: whether you are Issachar, Judah, Benjamin, Levi or Ephraim matters to him. That is the Catholic Church talking through him, remixing the word of God. Christ said he was not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel. The bloodline matters.

He quotes Paul about not getting into genealogies, but that was said while the temple was still standing and genealogies were being used to get into the temple. Now we have been destroyed and scattered and have lost our identity, and we have to find it out. And if genealogy did not matter, why does the New Testament start with one? Christians are idiots; they do not know how to read the Bible, so they come up with catchy cliches like race not grace and Hebrew hopscotch. When you forget your purpose and get caught up in the cares of this world, numbers and preeminence, you will get confounded by a negro like that. That is why we have to feed the sheep and cannot abandon our post.

sense.text:
He asks, what is the gospel? They try to call it Hebrew hopscotch when you can bounce through the Bible precept upon precept and get to the end and it makes perfect sense. They only say that because they cannot do it; they do not have the spirit of God to do it. They try to flip it on you and make you feel bad for actually knowing the word of God.

“And this gospel of the kingdom shall be preached in all the world for a witness.” Christ says this gospel. What is this gospel, the good news? The book of Acts shows it.

precepts.why:
“Be it known unto you therefore, men and brethren, that through this man is preached unto you the forgiveness of sins.” That is the gospel of the kingdom: Christ came to give you forgiveness of your sins. All twelve tribes had been cut off, in sin and idolatry, gone into slavery, and needed a savior, a sacrifice, that they might be forgiven.

“And by him all that believe are justified from all things, from which ye could not be justified by the law of Moses.” That is the gospel of the kingdom: that you could be justified in Christ, which you could not be under Moses.

There are Christians watching who will say all things means all people. Go back to who it was spoken to.

“Of this man’s seed hath God according to his promise raised unto Israel a Saviour, Jesus: When John had first preached before his coming the baptism of repentance to all the people of Israel.” Unto Israel; to all the people of Israel.

“And we declare unto you glad tidings.” Glad tidings is the gospel, the good news. “How that the promise which was made unto the fathers, God hath fulfilled the same unto us their children, in that he hath raised up Jesus again; as it is also written in the second psalm, Thou art my Son, this day have I begotten thee.”

That was good news to the Israelites scattered abroad: that they could be justified in all things they could not be justified in under the law of Moses, meaning sacrifice. That is the gospel of the kingdom that needed to be preached to all the Israelites scattered abroad.

And look at it again for the Christians who call it Hebrew hopscotch: “as it is also written.” The apostles went back to what was written.

What Christians call cherry-picking and Hebrew hopscotch, we understand as studying and understanding the word of God.

“And to this agree the words of the prophets; as it is written.” They had to go back and search: this was written here, so what happened in this place makes sense because the prophets wrote about it. That is precept upon precept, not Hebrew hopscotch. That is understanding the history and the things that must take place.

They do not have the spirit of the Lord and cannot do it, and want to shame us for having understanding and the spirit of God to go from Genesis to Revelation and give you the understanding thereof. We are going to keep going precept upon precept. That is why we have to feed the sheep.

sense.text:
“Wherefore the rather, brethren, give diligence.” Since we live in a time at war of ignorance, brother, you have to give diligence to your calling.

To give diligence to make your calling sure is an invitation to zealously live out your God-given purpose. That means be on fire: covet to prophesy. Believers are urged to put in intentional effort. Don’t just go through the motions because you are not where you think you should be; you are where God wants you to be, a prophet sent to save the people. Be intentional about it. And energetic effort: don’t be a boring teacher. As the Bishop and the Deacon say, you have to have some racial anger to be a good teacher. Put energy into it when you prophesy, because the people need it to wake up the soul that is asleep in them. Practice the virtues: faith, goodness, knowledge, self-control and love.

The result of diligence: practicing these protects a person from becoming spiritually blind or forgetting their purpose. When you give diligence you do not forget your purpose; you strive zealously to fulfil the mission. Actively reinforcing your faith is teaching, because that is what you were sent here to do; every prophet knows the feeling on cloud nine after teaching in the streets, no matter how long the ride home is. It gives stability and assurance that you will never fall from your purpose.

“To make your calling and election sure.” All of us ordained prophets by God to save the people make our calling and election sure by teaching them, saving them, prophesying, doing the work, on top of keeping the commandments. Keeping the commandments is the purpose of life; you are supposed to do that. But you are on another mission as a soldier of God: wake up the people, save them, give them warning. Give diligence to that. “For if ye do these things, ye shall never fall.”

And what is waiting on you? “For so an entrance shall be ministered unto you abundantly into the everlasting kingdom of our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ.”

When your mission is done you will hear the words, Well done, thou good and faithful servant, enter into the paradise prepared for you, because you as a brother, a soldier, a prophet of God, gave diligence to the mission that was at hand while you were upon the earth.

precepts.why:
What we are experiencing today, in all the silly foolishness online, is this: “Moreover this was not enough for them, that they erred in the knowledge of God; but whereas they lived in the great war of ignorance.”

We live in the time of great ignorance, and we are at war in it. One woman on a podcast says Genesis has God creating a world in our image, male and female, and that Jerusalem above being our mother means a mother and father in heaven, Elohim as male and female. The scripture does not say that; it says let us make man in our image. She made it up, and nobody fact-checked her, and our people say, I like that, I’m feeling that.

So we have to cast down those imaginations and fulfil the mission God placed us on here: teach his word and bring the tribes of Jacob back to him, so our people do not fall into this foolishness. That is why we must give diligence.
